title: What If Every Alligator Vanished? Swamps Would Dry Out

scenes.text: What if every alligator vanished? The first thing to go might be the water.
In the dry season, alligators dig holes by thrashing around, scooping out mud and clearing plants.
Those gator holes hold water when everything around them dries, a refuge for fish, turtles, birds, and mammals.
Take the alligators away and those refuges silt in. Wildlife loses its last pools in a drought.
Some turtles also incubate their eggs inside alligator nests, so they would lose their nurseries too.
That is why the Everglades calls the alligator a keystone species. Remove one animal and the swamp changes.
